Chapter 3: The Strength to Keep Going When It’s Hard
As Hafid kept moving forward on his journey, he unrolled the next scroll—and found a lesson that would really test his grit: the art of persistence.
You know, the world’s full of people who start out strong, all fired up—but the moment things get tough, they throw in the towel. Their dreams don’t fade because they’re impossible. Nope. It’s usually because they just don’t have the patience, or the strength, to see things through.
The scroll made something clear: setbacks and failures aren’t signs that you should quit. They’re actually invitations—opportunities to get stronger.
Hafid thought back to his early days in the marketplace, when every rejection felt personal. Every time someone said “no,” it chipped away at his confidence. He remembered just how tempting it was to walk away, to tell himself, “Maybe success is for someone else—not me.”
But this scroll encouraged him to keep pushing forward, no matter how many times he stumbled. And here’s the thing: persistence isn’t about being stubborn or just blindly hoping things will work out. It’s about learning from every experience, tweaking your approach, and refusing to let a temporary setback decide your future.
One afternoon, Hafid watched another merchant struggling to sell his goods. You could see the frustration on the guy’s face—every failed attempt made his voice a little sharper. Hafid recognized that look all too well. Instead of stepping in with advice, he just stood close by, quietly letting the man know he wasn’t alone.
Eventually, the merchant let out a long sigh and admitted he was ready to give up. That’s when Hafid shared his own story—not as a lecture, but just as a gentle reminder that everyone faces doubt. He talked about the wisdom from the scroll: that every big achievement is built on a solid foundation of perseverance.
The merchant listened. You could see his shoulders relax, realizing that maybe his struggle wasn’t unique after all.
With time, Hafid learned to see obstacles as chances to grow. Every challenge became a moment to practice resilience—a moment to prove to himself that he could keep going, even when he had no idea what would happen next.
And he started to notice something. The most successful people in the marketplace? They weren’t always the most talented or the most charming. They were the ones who showed up, day after day. The ones who refused to let disappointment become defeat.
Persistence, he realized, isn’t just for business. It matters in relationships, in personal growth, in every corner of life. The ability to keep moving forward—especially when things get tough—is what separates mediocrity from greatness.
Most people, Hafid saw, give up just before the breakthrough. They never know how close they were to making it.
The scroll’s message? It was simple, but powerful: keep going. The road might be long, and the rewards might not show up right away—but every step you take brings you closer to your goal.
In the end, it isn’t talent or luck that decides who succeeds. It’s that quiet strength—the willingness to keep trying, no matter what.
